title: Abstract 332: Effects of Fish Oil Enriched in Omega-11 Fatty Acid on Lipoprotein Metabolism in Healthy Adults

sections.abstract: <jats:p> <jats:bold>Background:</jats:bold> Fish oils enriched in omega-3 fatty acid possess anti-atherosclerotic properties; however, fish oils have diverse fatty acids, including long-chain monounsaturated fatty acids greater than 20 carbons (LCMUFA). </jats:p> <jats:p> <jats:bold>Aim:</jats:bold> Investigate effects of an omega-11-LCMUFA enriched fish oil (saury oil) on lipoprotein metabolism in healthy subjects. </jats:p> <jats:p> <jats:bold>Methods:</jats:bold> To understand effects of saury oil, we compared it to a control oil matched in the total omega-3 fatty acids and MUFA (C18:1, oleic acid) in a prospective double-blinded randomized crossover study in 37 healthy subjects. Extensive cardiometabolic parameters have been analyzed at each 4 visits (n=30). Vascular function was estimated with ABI and cardio-ankle vascular index (CAVI). </jats:p> <jats:p> <jats:bold>Results:</jats:bold> Enrolled healthy subjects had a mean age of 34.8 years and BMI of 24.3 and no significant changes in other screening laboratory values. Treatment with 12g/day of saury (LCMUFA: 3.5g; omega-3: 2.1g) or control oil (MUFA: 4.5g; omega-3: 2.4g) on average increased TC (4.3%) and HDL-C (6.2%) compared to the baseline, whereas LDL-C, sdLDL, oxLDL, TG-rich LDL (LDL-TG) and TG did not change significantly. However, NMR lipid analyses for control oil supplementation detected more robust LDLp increase in comparison to saury oil (1537.2 ± 557.7 vs. 1423.2 ± 639.5, respectively) (p=0.004). TG-rich lipoproteins, specifically small and medium, were significantly decreased in both treatments as compared to baseline. VLDLp was significantly lowered with both interventions, whereas saury oil decreased ApoB more significantly as compared to control oil (76.7 ± 35.1 vs. 81.8 ± 30.6, respectively) (p=0.01). Although, saury oil supplementation increased cholesterol efflux capacity (CEC) by 8.5%, HDLp was significantly decreased compared to baseline (p=0.014) mostly by large HDLp. There was no change in CAVI but significantly lower ABI in both treatments as compared to baseline. Finally, we did not observe significant changes in safety profile of both treatments. </jats:p> <jats:p> <jats:bold>Conclusions:</jats:bold> Both saury and control oils enriched in omega-3 fatty acid showed some similarities in their effect on lipoprotein metabolism; however, saury oil had better improvement in HDL function, as well as decrease in LDLp and ApoB, which is likely attributed to LCMUFA. </jats:p>
